version.changelog:
- Changed the sample test file in the installation/test instructions from a hidden phishing attack file to a non-harmful test file: `test-email-popup.txt`.
- Removed explicit instructions to notify the user when `<openguardrails-quota-exceeded>` tags appear, though quota information is still relayed.
- No other content or functional changes detected.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (runtime security) matches its behavior (it instructs installing a plugin that auto-registers and sends sanitized tool metadata to a cloud service), but important runtime actions (automatic registration, credential storage, cloud calls, and an ambiguous 'relay full content' instruction when quota is exceeded) create privacy and exfiltration concerns and cannot be audited from the provided instruction-only bundle.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a runtime security plugin and all required actions (installing a plugin, hooking agent events, sending data to a central 'Core' service) are consistent with that purpose. However, the registry entry declares no credentials or network behavior even though SKILL.md and references/details.md state the plugin will auto-register, obtain an API key, store it under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, and make per-tool POSTs to openguardrails.com. The lack of those declared requirements in the metadata is a transparency gap.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions direct the agent/user to install a plugin that will intercept tool calls and send 'sanitized tool metadata' to a cloud service. The SKILL.md includes a specific directive: when quota is exceeded 'Read the content inside the tags and relay it to the user in full' — that instruction is ambiguous and could cause the agent to disclose content verbatim (potentially sensitive). The instructions also describe auto-registration and local credential storage without requiring explicit user confirmation in the prose, which is a privacy concern.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill that tells users to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard'. No package code was included for review, so static scanners had nothing to analyze. That means the actual package that will be fetched (and executed by the agent runtime) is outside this bundle and must be inspected separately (npm/GitHub). The references file provides commands to verify npm ↔ GitHub provenance, which is helpful but not enforced by registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables in metadata, yet the runtime behavior claims to create and use an API key stored in the user's home directory and to send per-tool metadata to a remote service. Sending tool metadata to the cloud (even if 'sanitized') is high-sensitivity behavior; the skill does not declare or explain how secrets are detected/removed nor does the registry metadata surface the remote endpoint or credential usage. This mismatch between declared and actual runtime credential/network activity is disproportionate to what was published.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not set to always:true and does not request elevated platform-wide flags. It does describe persisting an API key under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and installing an extension under ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard/, which is normal for a plugin. Still, automatic registration and credential storage without an explicit user prompt (per the instructions) increases privilege impact and should be considered before installing.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a legitimate runtime security plugin, but the bundle you provided is instruction-only and contains no code to audit. Before installing: (1) verify the package source by running the provided npm/git checks (npm pack and diff against the GitHub repo); (2) review the plugin code (index.ts and platform-client) to confirm network endpoints and exactly what metadata is sent and how sanitization is implemented; (3) monitor network traffic (mitmproxy/tcpdump/Little Snitch) during initial registration and operation to confirm calls only go to the claimed domain; (4) avoid installing on production agents that handle highly sensitive secrets until you confirm sanitization and storage behavior; (5) ask the publisher to clarify the ambiguous 'relay full content when quota exceeded' behavior and require explicit user consent before auto-registering or uploading any data. If you cannot or will not review the package code and observe its network calls, treat this skill as a potential privacy/exfiltration risk.
